# Seerr

Seerr is where people ask for films and series. It passes their requests to Sonarr and
Radarr. Mediaplane runs the upstream image, unmodified (see
[ADR 0006](../../docs/adr/0006-seerr-as-the-requests-app.md)).

## What Mediaplane sets

- **Image:** `ghcr.io/seerr-team/seerr:v3.5.0`
- **Digest:** `sha256:27602401178d54f1964442287b9f23f67a3fa2252645ee8065839ea1c3f69e45`
- **Architectures:** amd64, arm64
- **Ports:** 5055/tcp (web), published as `network.bind` says; `apps.seerr.port` moves the host port
- **Volumes:** `<home>/appdata/seerr` → `/app/config`
- **Runs as:** uid 1000, fixed by the image. Mediaplane gives `<home>/appdata/seerr` to 1000:1000 before the app starts
- **Health check:** `wget -qO- http://localhost:5055/api/v1/status > /dev/null || exit 1`, every 30s (timeout 10s, 5 retries, 60s to start)
- **Secrets:** `apiKey`: 32 random hex characters, generated once and kept in `state/secrets.json`
- **API:** on its `web` port, which Mediaplane reaches over the stack's wiring network, with `apiKey` in the `X-Api-Key` header
- **Managed in the app:** `seerr.media_server`: fields `seerr.media_server.hostname` (fixed), `seerr.media_server.port` (fixed), `seerr.media_server.libraries`; the secret `apiKey`, checked and never shown. `seerr.media_server_plex`: fields `seerr.media_server_plex.hostname` (fixed), `seerr.media_server_plex.port` (fixed), `seerr.media_server_plex.libraries`. `seerr.server_sonarr`: fields `seerr.server_sonarr.hostname` (fixed), `seerr.server_sonarr.port` (fixed), `seerr.server_sonarr.activeProfile`, `seerr.server_sonarr.activeDirectory`, `seerr.server_sonarr.isDefault`; the secret `apiKey`, checked and never shown. `seerr.server_radarr`: fields `seerr.server_radarr.hostname` (fixed), `seerr.server_radarr.port` (fixed), `seerr.server_radarr.activeProfile`, `seerr.server_radarr.activeDirectory`, `seerr.server_radarr.isDefault`; the secret `apiKey`, checked and never shown. `seerr.setup`: fields `seerr.setup.initialized` (fixed)
- **Needs:** `media-server`, `pvr`
- **Provides:** `requests`
- **Also turns on:** nothing

## What Mediaplane does today

With Jellyfin as the media server (with Plex, see below):

- **Its first sign-in, before its web UI is published.** Until someone signs in, anyone
  who reaches Seerr can sign in through a Jellyfin of their own and be its admin. So
  `apply` starts Seerr with no port published, and once Jellyfin is set up, signs Seerr in
  through Jellyfin as the shared admin: that makes the shared admin Seerr's admin, and
  Jellyfin, at `jellyfin:8096` with no URL base and no TLS, its media server. It signs out
  again at once, and only then publishes Seerr. `plan` lists it under `First-run setup:`.
  Seerr counts as set up only when its `settings.json` says so (`mediaServerType`) and
  Mediaplane's record does (`setUp` in `state/secrets.json`, a list of app names).
  Mediaplane's sign-in must be Seerr's first: it asks Seerr whose the session is, and
  anything but its admin (its first user) means someone else signed in first, even in the
  moment before. Mediaplane then signs out, and Seerr is treated as set up by someone
  else: it stays unpublished, `apply` stops, and the error gives the safe ways out first.
  This holds when `apply` runs the stack; the threat model lists what voids it, such as a
  Seerr whose appdata is reset outside `apply`:
  [T16](../../docs/security/threat-model.md#t16-someone-else-finishes-an-apps-first-run-setup).
- **A Seerr set up before Slice 6,** by hand, has no record. The first `apply` starts
  it unpublished once and checks it with its key, never the password. It is
  Mediaplane's only when its admin (its first user) is the Jellyfin login
  `admin.username` names and its Jellyfin is `jellyfin:8096`, with no URL base and no
  TLS; then it is recorded and published. Otherwise it stays unpublished, and the
  [runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md) has the ways out.
- **Its login** is Jellyfin's: on Seerr's sign-in page, choose Jellyfin and use the
  shared admin login (`mediaplane credentials`). It follows Jellyfin's, so a change of
  `admin.password` reaches Seerr once it reaches Jellyfin. Seerr makes a user for anyone
  else who signs in with a Jellyfin account, as it always does.
- **Its API key.** Generated once, kept in `state/secrets.json`, and passed in
  `API_KEY`, which Seerr takes at every start (its `settings.json` keeps the first). It
  works once Seerr has its admin.
- **Its media server** (`seerr.media_server`): Jellyfin, at its service and port, with
  no URL base and no TLS (either, set in Seerr, counts as Jellyfin moved, and `apply`
  puts it back), and the Movies and Shows libraries enabled. A library you enable in
  Seerr stays yours. Seerr uses the key it made itself in Jellyfin as it signed in
  (named `Seerr` in Jellyfin's dashboard): Mediaplane checks that it works, and gives
  Seerr its own Jellyfin key only when Jellyfin refuses Seerr's, or Jellyfin moves,
  when Seerr's libraries are synced again too. Seerr shows that key in clear: Mediaplane
  keeps it out of all it prints and records. Seerr sets Jellyfin's id (`serverId`) at
  its first sign-in and on each link it saves: a link with an empty id reads as not
  linked, and `apply` links it again.
- **Its Sonarr and Radarr servers** (`seerr.server_sonarr`, `seerr.server_radarr`), each
  while the stack runs the arr, named `Sonarr (Mediaplane)` and `Radarr (Mediaplane)`: the
  arr at its service and port, with its key, its root folder, a quality profile, and set
  as the default, so requests go there. The profile is `HD-1080p`, else `Any`, else the
  arr's first, unless you name one (below). The rest is what Seerr's own web UI gives a
  new server, but with season folders for Sonarr, as Sonarr's own default (Radarr's has
  none), and stays yours after. Seerr shows the arr's key in clear; Mediaplane checks it
  with Seerr's own test of the server, which calls the arr with it, and keeps it out of
  all it prints and records, a key typed in Seerr by hand too. Mediaplane sends the arr's
  key only to the arr's own address in the stack, with no URL base, never to a host or
  URL base read from Seerr: a server Seerr holds with TLS or a URL base counts as
  changed, and `apply` puts it back. Seerr is wired after Prowlarr, when the stack has it.
- **With Plex as the media server,** the same, but:
  - **Its first sign-in** is with your Plex token (`POST /api/v1/auth/plex`), once Plex is
    claimed for your account, before Seerr's web UI is published. That makes your plex.tv
    account Seerr's admin, and Plex its media server. It signs out again at once. As
    through Jellyfin, that sign-in must be Seerr's first, its admin's, or Seerr stays
    unpublished. A Seerr set up already is checked with its key, and never signed in to,
    which would give your token to whoever set it up: it is Mediaplane's only when its
    admin's plex.tv account is the one plex.tv says your token is, and its Plex is unset
    or `plex:32400`, without TLS. Otherwise it stays unpublished, and the
    [runbook](../../docs/runbooks/wiring-failed.md) has the ways out.
  - **Its login** is your own plex.tv account: on Seerr's sign-in page, choose Plex.
    Seerr makes a user for anyone else who signs in with a plex.tv account that your
    Plex is shared with, as it always does.
  - **Its media server** (`seerr.media_server_plex`): Plex, at `plex:32400` without TLS,
    with the Movies and TV Shows libraries enabled. Seerr reaches Plex with its admin's
    token, yours, which it keeps from its first sign-in: the link holds no key of
    Mediaplane's. Plex with TLS, set in Seerr, counts as Plex moved, and `apply` puts it
    back. A link with an empty Plex id (`machineId`) reads as not linked, and `apply`
    links it again. It comes after Plex's name and both libraries. A library you enable
    in Seerr stays yours.
- **Its setup, finished** (`seerr.setup`): once its links are in place, Mediaplane sends
  Seerr's `initialize`, so it stops offering its admin the setup wizard.
- **Its user.** Seerr's image runs as uid 1000, the `node` user. So before it starts,
  Mediaplane gives `appdata/seerr` to 1000:1000, with a throwaway container of Seerr's own
  image.
- **What it needs.** A media server, which always runs, and Sonarr or Radarr. Listing
  Seerr does not turn either on: list one of them too, or `plan` reports an error.
- **`init: true`,** as Seerr's own Compose example has it.
- **`LOG_LEVEL=info`.**
- **Its web UI,** published as `network.bind` says, once it is set up.

## Drift and Keep mine

- **What drift reports.** `mediaplane drift`, and `plan`, report a change made in
  Seerr's web UI to what Mediaplane manages here, listed above under "Managed in the
  app": what Mediaplane set, and what Seerr holds now. A secret is checked with
  Seerr's own test, and named, never shown. `apply` puts each back.
- **Keeping yours.** `mediaplane keep seerr.<resource>.<field>`, as drift names it,
  keeps what Seerr holds instead: it adds the line under `overrides:` in `stack.yaml`,
  and `apply` then leaves it. A field marked `(fixed)` above, and a secret, can't be
  kept. `mediaplane keep seerr.server_radarr` stops Mediaplane managing a resource deleted
  in Seerr. The [drift runbook](../../docs/runbooks/drift-reported.md) says more.
- **A library turned off in Seerr,** kept (`seerr.media_server.libraries`, or
  `media_server_plex`): Mediaplane then enables only the libraries kept, and the others
  are yours, to turn on or off. A library Mediaplane no longer manages in Jellyfin or
  Plex is never enabled by it.
- **Where Seerr sends a key** is fixed: the host and port of its media server and of its
  Sonarr and Radarr servers. Drift reports a change to one, and `apply` puts the stack's
  own address back; Mediaplane's tests of a server are aimed there, and Seerr's list of
  Jellyfin's users is asked only while Seerr holds the stack's address. `keep` reads a
  server's profile from what was applied, rather than run Seerr's test.
- **A server's profile, root folder or default,** kept
  (`seerr.server_sonarr.activeProfile`, `activeDirectory`, `isDefault`), stays; a
  profile is kept by its name, as text. While Seerr's key for an arr is known refused,
  neither drift nor `plan` asks Seerr to test the arr for its profiles: a key known wrong
  leaves no new line in Seerr's log, nor in the arr's. Its setup
  (`seerr.setup.initialized`) is fixed: Seerr can't be taken back to its setup wizard.

## Not built yet

- **Slice 10b:** a way to give Seerr a new Plex token: it keeps the one it signed in with.

See the [roadmap](../../docs/plans/m1-roadmap.md).

## Changing it

- **In `stack.yaml`,** under `apps.seerr`, you can set `port`, `version`, `env` and
  `enabled: false`. A different `version` is an untested combination, and `plan` warns
  about it. See the [`stack.yaml` reference](../../docs/reference/stack-yaml.md).
- **The quality profiles** it requests with: `apps.seerr.sonarr_profile` and
  `apps.seerr.radarr_profile`, each a profile's name, as the arr shows it. A name the
  arr doesn't have fails, listing those it has.
- **What Mediaplane manages** (the fields above) is put back by the next `apply` when
  changed in Seerr: its Jellyfin or Plex, its libraries, and each server's host, port,
  profile, root folder and default, unless you keep it (see above).
- **Anything else** goes in `compose.override.yaml` in the Mediaplane home.

## Known issues

- **A request needs the internet.** Seerr looks up films and series on TMDB, an outside
  service, and the arrs look them up again on their own: Mediaplane's tests stop at the
  links, and Seerr's own test of each.
- **A failing check is logged.** `plan` and `apply` check Seerr's servers and its key for
  Jellyfin; each check that fails logs a line in Seerr's log (Settings, Logs), and one
  with a key the arr refuses, a line in the arr's.
- **Jellyfin keeps a key named `Seerr`,** which Seerr made as it first signed in, and a
  device of Seerr's sign-in. Both are Seerr's own: leave them.
- **Removing it needs `sudo`.** `appdata/seerr` belongs to uid 1000, so unless you are
  that user, deleting it needs `sudo`.
